# Debrief: Istio, Envoy

These clips cover Istio's evolution from Envoy sidecars to ambient mesh with ztunnel, GitHub-scale production lessons, ambient migration tradeoffs, and ways to extend and migrate onto Envoy. ([Evolution or Revolution: Istio as the Network Platform for Cloud Native · 4:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4K6s5y8HoBc&t=264s); [Istio in Production: Expected Value, Results, and Effort at GitHub Scale · 4:12](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2fXwQylR2lw&t=252s); [The Good, The Ugly, and The Bad: Leaving Sidecars Behind with Istio Ambient Mesh · 21:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ToKv7JntLvY&t=1319s))

## Top 3 takeaways

1. Istio ran only Envoy sidecars for years; sidecars proved mesh value but hurt resource use and upgrades, since every pod restarted to upgrade. Ztunnel, a per-node L4 proxy for mTLS, was introduced in response. ([Evolution or Revolution: Istio as the Network Platform for Cloud Native · 4:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4K6s5y8HoBc&t=264s))
2. Ztunnel is a Rust-based, much smaller codebase offering higher throughput and lower latency than full Envoy for L4 routing and mTLS. It is pluggable; Calico deploys Istio with its own ztunnel fork. ([Evolution or Revolution: Istio as the Network Platform for Cloud Native · 13:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4K6s5y8HoBc&t=788s))
3. Moving to ambient with Gateway API can break tooling: cert-manager needed an experimental feature, and Argo Rollouts needed a Gateway API plugin. Expect to update surrounding tools, not just Istio. ([The Good, The Ugly, and The Bad: Leaving Sidecars Behind with Istio Ambient Mesh · 21:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ToKv7JntLvY&t=1319s))

## Action items

- [ ] Inventory tools that touch traffic or certificates, such as cert-manager and Argo Rollouts, and check whether each needs Gateway API support or plugins before trying ambient. ([The Good, The Ugly, and The Bad: Leaving Sidecars Behind with Istio Ambient Mesh · 21:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ToKv7JntLvY&t=1319s))
- [ ] Evaluate ztunnel for L4 mTLS needs, comparing its throughput and latency against your current Envoy sidecars, and note that ambient multicluster is now in beta. ([Evolution or Revolution: Istio as the Network Platform for Cloud Native · 13:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4K6s5y8HoBc&t=788s); [Istio in Production: Expected Value, Results, and Effort at GitHub Scale · 21:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2fXwQylR2lw&t=1278s))
- [ ] If you need custom Envoy behavior, prototype it with dynamic modules or external processing rather than waiting on Envoy release cadence. ([Envoy in the Era of Agentic Workloads · 19:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HvX4nGkhfZw&t=1188s))

## Watch together (9 min)

1. [Evolution or Revolution: Istio as the Network Platform for Cloud Native · 4:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4K6s5y8HoBc&t=264s) (1:25), Mitch Connors, Daniel Grimm: Explains why Istio moved from sidecars to ztunnel.
2. [The Good, The Ugly, and The Bad: Leaving Sidecars Behind with Istio Ambient Mesh · 21:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ToKv7JntLvY&t=1319s) (1:21), Alfonso Ming, Jorge Turrado: Concrete ambient migration pain points with Gateway API tooling.
3. [Istio in Production: Expected Value, Results, and Effort at GitHub Scale · 21:18](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2fXwQylR2lw&t=1278s) (2:18), Mitch Connors, Golnaz Rouhi: GitHub-scale lessons: ambient multicluster beta, platform thinking, community cooperation.
4. [Evolution or Revolution: Istio as the Network Platform for Cloud Native · 13:08](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4K6s5y8HoBc&t=788s) (1:19), Mitch Connors, Daniel Grimm: Ztunnel performance benefits and CNI ecosystem adoption.
5. [Envoy in the Era of Agentic Workloads · 19:48](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HvX4nGkhfZw&t=1188s) (2:25), Yan Avlasov, Erica Hughberg: Advice on extending Envoy via dynamic modules and external processes.
